intro: Lazur is an AI assistant for lawyers on the Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ in Word or Outlook and ask it to sum up the page, find a clause or draft the reply. Follow your firm's rules on client data first.
tldr: Ask “where's the termination clause?” and Lazur points at it on screen.
Get the page on screen summed up out loud.
Dictate emails and notes with fn in any app.
Check your firm's policy on AI tools and client data first.

painPoints.title: Long documents
painPoints.text: Finding the one clause that matters in a 40-page agreement takes scrolling and searching.

painPoints.title: Email volume
painPoints.text: Status updates to clients and opposing counsel, all day, mostly the same shape.

painPoints.title: Deadlines
painPoints.text: Filing dates and calls that live in your head until they are in a calendar.

day.result: Reads the page on screen and gives you the gist out loud.
Points at it on the page you have open.

day.result: Writes the draft in Outlook for you to edit.

day.result: Starts a timer in the notch.

blocks.text: Lazur sees your screen only while you hold the shortcut. The audio and that one screenshot are sent to AI providers to answer you and are not stored, and are never used to train models. That may or may not fit your firm's rules. Check them, and do not use it on matters where it would not.

faq.question: Is Lazur approved for legal work?
faq.answer: Lazur makes no compliance claims for legal practice. Read the [privacy policy](/privacy) and check your firm's rules before using it with client material.

faq.question: Does Lazur work in every app?
faq.answer: Yes. It works on top of any Mac app: Mail, Slack, Chrome, Word, Figma, Cursor and the rest.

faq.question: Is it always listening?
faq.answer: No. It listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot are not stored.
